moat_against: Subscale network (~1,400-1,500 properties) vs Marriott/Hilton at 8,000-9,000+ — weaker owner distribution and loyalty network effects
No evidenced high ROIC: roic_proxy and gross margin are null in fundamentals.json (operating income untagged); OE/share was negative in 2020 and $0.89 in 2025
Cyclical lodging demand — revenue fell from $5,020M (2019) to $2,066M (2020)
Leverage: net debt $3,491M is 9.4x normalized OE; buybacks at prices far above IV shrink the count without creating per-share value
moat_for: World of Hyatt loyalty — highest-value major hotel points currency, high-end guest base
Luxury/lifestyle brand portfolio (Park Hyatt, Alila, Inclusive Collection) skewed to high-value guests
Long-dated fee contracts — 50-year management agreements on the Playa resorts sold in Dec 2025
Pipeline ~154,000 rooms (+10% YoY) and net rooms growth ~4-6% supporting fee growth
moat_justification: Strong luxury/lifestyle brands and World of Hyatt — the highest-value major hotel loyalty currency — plus long-dated management contracts (50-year terms on the sold Playa resorts) and a 154,000-room pipeline, but subscale at ~1,400-1,500 properties vs Marriott/Hilton at 8,000-9,000+, no filed ROIC/gross-margin series in fundamentals.json (operating income untagged, roic_proxy null), and a volatile, thin OE record (negative in 2020, $0.89/share in 2025) that does not evidence returns well above cost of capital through a cycle.
name: Hyatt Hotels Corp
one_liner: Quality lodging franchisor in an asset-light transition, moat 5/10 — does not clear 15% at $169.13: weighted IRR 5.35%, weighted IV@15% $36.99, and even the super-bull case (7.40% IRR) is Tier D; clears 15% only below ~$36.99.
